Team —

Kicking off this week’s demand convergence thread for Oct -> Nov planning. Goal: reconcile sales pipeline commits for Dedicated capacity with finance run‑rate and infra constraints so we have a single ask to engineering by EOW.

Quick context: Nova Robotics deal (ND-2026-1147) is moving to LOI and they’ve asked for a Reserved pool starting early Jan. Sales forecast currently shows a 16k token-hr/month committed load in Q1, but that’s not yet capacity-approved.

Please reply with the following by EOD Wed:
- Laura: an updated slot estimate (GPU hours/week) for current pipeline + a tight/likely/optimistic view
- Karthik: any hard constraints on allocation (min safety buffer, provisioning lead times) + suggestions for temporary mitigations
- Ben: confirm finance assumptions for unit cost and any approval cadence we should expect for commits > $X/month
- Marissa: any deal-level asks/SLAs that would change capacity profile (burst slots, reserved vs burst mix)

I’ve attached the current pipeline export (see related_links) — I’ll combine replies into the MA plan and circulate. If you need more context from Hugo at Nova, I can loop him in but prefer internal alignment first.

Thanks,
Priyom

- Tight: 9.8k token-hr/month -> ~2.4 GPU-days/week (on A100-equivalent) once batching assumed
- Likely: 13.4k token-hr/month -> ~3.3 GPU-days/week

- Unit cost assumptions: we’re modeling a blended marginal cost of $0.55 / GPU-hour for burst and $0.35 / GPU-hour for reserved (post‑commit). For initial commit sizing we need a 6‑month cost proforma to take to revenue ops — can someone own that?
- Approval cadence: for committed spend > $40k/month we need VP Finance sign-off plus legal review for contract T&Cs. That means realistic lead time is ~3 weeks for approvals once SOW is in legal.

On Fri, Oct 29, 2026 at 09:14 AM Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Priyom — attaching a quick breakdown (pipeline-breakdown.pdf) with three scenarios. Summary here: 

Good notes. Two operational flags:

1) Provisioning lead time — cold capacity (new rack/node ordering + image bake) is ~6 weeks; warm reallocation (move reserved units between accounts) is ~2–3 days but impacted by current burn windows.
2) Safety buffer — we should keep a 10% fleet safety margin for scheduled business-critical reserved customers (this is non-negotiable for SLA). For deals that can tolerate burst, we can temporarily route to higher-latency burst pools.

Mitigations I recommend:
- For Nova: start with a split 70% reserved / 30% burst for the first 90 days; reserve only after legal/finance sign-off confirmed.
- If Ben needs cost smoothing, we can offer a ramp schedule in the contract (1/3 commit->2/3 commit over 3 months).

I’ll check infra calendar for available reallocation windows next week and report back.

—Karthik
